original_question: For a Pinwheel tiling of the plane, place a point mass at the natural reference point of each tile and consider the resulting Dirac comb. Its diffraction measure is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation and is known to have circular symmetry. Determine where the sharp rings occur in this diffraction measure and compute their intensities.
target_in_paper: Section 2.3, Problem 2.3.1: "Determine the position of sharp rings in the diffraction measure of a Pinwheel Tiling and their intensity."
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely. It correctly uses a Pinwheel Tiling of the plane, places a point mass at the natural tile reference point, forms the associated Dirac comb, identifies the diffraction measure as the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation, notes the circular symmetry of the diffraction, and asks for the locations and intensities of the sharp rings. That is essentially the content of Problem 2.3.1.
missing_details: The paper fixes the geometric setting more explicitly: a Pinwheel Tiling is a tiling of R^2 by congruent copies of the right triangle with side lengths 1, 2, and sqrt(5), arising from the Conway-Radin inflation/subdivision rule.
The reference point is not arbitrary: the paper's natural choice is the point with coordinates (1/2, 1/2) relative to the right-angled corner of the triangular tile.
The measure is the uniform Dirac comb on those reference points; no additional weights are introduced.
Because all Pinwheel Tilings are locally indistinguishable, the diffraction problem is intended to be independent of which Pinwheel Tiling is chosen.

The paper distinguishes planar pure point diffraction from 'sharp rings': by circular symmetry, the only planar pure point atom is the trivial one at the origin, coming from density 1, while sharp rings are continuous in the plane but pure point in the radial variable.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should explicitly target the nontrivial rings away from the origin, i.e. the radii at which ring components occur and their intensities.
The possible absolutely continuous part of the diffraction is not part of this problem; it is posed separately as Problem 2.3.2 and should not be merged into the refined question.
There are no ambient-ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' conditions in this problem; the hidden assumptions are geometric and measure-theoretic instead.
refined_question: Let P be any Pinwheel Tiling of R^2 by congruent copies of the right triangle with side lengths 1, 2, and sqrt(5), and let Lambda be the associated set of reference points obtained by placing one point at (1/2, 1/2) in tile coordinates based at the right-angled vertex of each tile. Form the uniform Dirac comb omega = sum_{x in Lambda} delta_x, and let gamma-hat be its diffraction measure, i.e. the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation of omega. Since gamma-hat is circularly symmetric and its only planar pure point atom is the trivial one at the origin, determine the nontrivial sharp rings of gamma-hat: identify the radii r > 0 for which gamma-hat has a ring component supported on the circle {k in R^2 : |k| = r}, and determine the corresponding ring intensities.
justification: The draft is targeting the pinwheel-diffraction problem in Section 2.3, not a broader neighboring question. That section defines the Pinwheel Tiling, specifies the natural reference point and the associated uniform Dirac comb, records that the diffraction measure is circularly symmetric and that the only planar pure point part is the trivial atom at the origin, explains that 'sharp rings' correspond to being pure point in the radial direction, and then states Problem 2.3.1 verbatim as determining the positions of those rings and their intensity. The nearby Problem 2.3.2 separately asks about an absolutely continuous component, so a faithful rewrite should remain narrowly focused on the sharp-ring support and intensities.
